title: What the Bar-headed Goose carries

is_this_you.pressure: When the climb turns steep you stay low and follow the ground. You get over by inches, then let people believe you flew straight across.
is_this_you.love: You keep faith on a seasonal clock. Gone for months, you still land where you promised.
is_this_you.cost: Some years you stay by a lake that stopped feeding you, because you once said you would.

opener.text: A Han envoy named Su Wu was held by the Xiongnu and made to herd sheep by Lake Baikal for 19 years [s7] [s8]. When his captors claimed he was dead, a Han official said the emperor had shot a wild goose with Su Wu's letter tied to its foot [s7] [s8]. The ruse set him free [s8]. It gave Chinese the idiom 雁足傳書 (yàn zú chuán shū), a goose carries the letter [s7]. You were born a Sagittarius in a Goat year. The sheep and the goose meet in you.

howto: Three parts. Take them one wingbeat at a time.

tabs.label: The high pass
tabs.intro: Fire aimed at the far side. Earth that keeps going.

rows.text: Sagittarius is mutable Fire, ruled by Jupiter, the curious and wandering sign [s1]. The Goat is yin Earth, gentle on the surface and tough inside [s2] [s4]. You aim at the far side of the mountain and still want the flock fed.

Tracked bar-headed geese crossed the Himalayas northbound in one push of about seven to eight hours [s10]. Most flights hug the ground at about 4,500 to 5,500 meters, rising and falling with each ridge [s11] [s12]. You follow every rise and dip of a problem until you are over it.

One data logger caught a single goose at 7,290 meters, on one brief flight [s12]. Taller stories about this bird rest on a second-hand sighting from 1961 [s15]. Part of you enjoys the taller version. The Goat in you knows the low road got you across.

tabs.label: The letter
tabs.intro: Word carried home across the distance.

rows.text: From the Western Han on, a wild goose, 雁 (yàn), was the Chinese betrothal gift, because it migrates at the same time every year [s9]. It promised the couple would keep faith [s9]. You love on that clock. You fly far, and you come back when you said you would.
Sagittarius can be tactless [s1]. The Goat can cling [s4]. So you dodge the fight, then say the blunt true thing from altitude. Land first, then speak.
Translation, diplomacy and expedition work all suit the envoy in you.

tabs.label: Who flies in your line
tabs.intro: Three who keep your wingbeat. One who would turn the skein around.
tabs.love_lead: In love you commit slowly, then keep the season. You need someone who lets you fly far and waits where you land. The old wheel gives you three of those.

easy.why: The Pronghorn (Aries, Horse year) is your secret friend, since the Horse is the Goat's hidden ally, and Aries is Fire like you [s3] [s1].
The Paradise Riflebird (Leo, Horse year) is the same secret friend, with Leo Fire to match yours [s3] [s1].
The Golden Pheasant (Leo, Rabbit year) shares your trine of Rabbit, Goat and Pig, and Leo is Fire too [s3] [s1].

hard.why: The hard one is the Three-wattled Bellbird (Gemini, Ox year): the Ox clashes with the Goat, and Gemini sits opposite Sagittarius [s3] [s1].

story.text: In Hindu tradition the hamsa carries Saraswati, goddess of knowledge and the arts, and later writers said it could separate milk from water [s5] [s6]. In 1979 the ornithologist Salim Ali argued that the poet Kalidasa's hamsa was the bar-headed goose [s5]. Others read it as a swan [s5]. You keep the milk and leave the water.

closing: Fly as far as the year asks. Then land where you promised, on time, with the letter still dry.
